svg.title: A-104 Penthouse Plan — Detached Villa
svg.text: PERGOLA OVER — CARRIED ACROSS THE ROOF TO THE NORTH TERRACE
CANTILEVER CARRIED TO THE TOP — 2.00 m WEST → 1.50 m EAST
Masonry wall cut by section — 200 mm
Internal stud or block partition, 120 mm
Single leaf door, swing shown to opening side
Glazed opening — arched head where noted
Element above the cut plane (pergola, slab
1. Draft for comment. A two-bedroom apartment between two
terraces, with its own front door. 58.6 m² indoors, 63.1
m² of terrace to the south and 14.2 m² to the north.
2. The pergola is what joins them: a band on each terrace
against the apartment, with its beams carried across the
apartment's roof between. The terraces are open to the sky
3. The apartment runs wall to wall because it has to. Two
bedrooms sit north of the stair side by side, and the only
line to divide them on is the spine, which leaves 4.51 and
4.09 m. Take 1.50 m off the east for a covered walk and
the second bedroom drops to 2.59 m wide, which is not a
4. The stair ends at y 12.42 and cannot move, so the
bedrooms' depth and the north terrace come out of the same
4.58 m. Flush north gives 18.5 m² bedrooms and no terrace
at all; the north wall at 15.50 gives 12.0 and 11.4 m² and
a 14.2 m² terrace. Both beds turn sideways in a 2.66 m
5. The south wall sits on the column grid at y 8.46, bearing
on the beam between the columns at x 12.65, 17.46 and
21.85; the third floor under it is an open living area.
East and west it sits on the walls below.
6. The site plan, section A—A and the A-300 enlargements are
Preliminary design issue — not for construction.
Do not scale; work to figured dimensions only.
